title: Highest temperature in London on August 1?
description:

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current high-pressure patterns and subsidence over southern England are supporting clear skies and light winds, enabling daytime solar heating to push London’s maximum temperature on August 1 toward 25–27 °C according to the latest Met Office and BBC runs. Model consensus highlights modest warm advection from the continent tempered by a fresher northwesterly flow, keeping values near or slightly above the long-term early-August average of ~22 °C without triggering the stronger heat advection seen earlier in the warm 2026 summer. eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from Météo-France and European models show the primary driver of trader sentiment as uncertainty in peak afternoon temperatures for Paris on August 1 amid an ongoing European heat wave. High-pressure dominance and southerly flow support values near seasonal norms plus 3–6°C, yet model spread on cloud cover, timing of any seabreeze influence, and urban heat island amplification keeps 28°C and 29°C nearly tied at market-implied odds of 33% and 34%. Resolution hinges on the official Météo-France maximum recorded at standard stations, with fresh model runs expected in the next 24–48 hours likely to narrow the distribution around the 28–30°C cluster.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Marine layer moderation and onshore flow are the dominant factors capping Los Angeles highs near 81–83 °F on August 1, 2026.** National Weather Service guidance highlights patchy morning fog followed by gradual clearing, yielding a forecast high near 81 °F at representative coastal and basin sites, while broader heat-ridge conditions produce mid-90s readings farther inland. This contrast arises from strengthened sea-breeze circulation and a persistent marine inversion that limits daytime mixing and advects cooler Pacific air onshore, differentiating the tightly bunched 80–83 °F outcomes. Recent model runs show only modest disagreements on the exact timing of fog dissipation and wind speeds, which directly influences whether the daily maximum settles at 80–81 °F or edges into the low 80s. Historical climatology for early August supports this range when onshore flow dominates, and traders appear to weight the latest NWS and ensemble guidance heavily given the proximity to resolution.
